D021-D022_h001.question:
I’ve always cared about staying healthy—nursing taught me that—but lately, things feel harder to manage. I lost my husband two years ago, and without him… meals just don’t feel necessary anymore. I used to cook for us both, but now I hardly eat. I’ve cut out bread, rice, anything starchy—I just can’t stomach the thought of it. Fats too. I know my body needs fuel, but the idea of gaining even a pound makes my chest tighten. I weigh myself every morning, sometimes more. If the number goes up, I’ll skip lunch or redo my stretches.  

There are times—more than I’d admit—when I eat a lot all at once, like a whole box of cookies, fast, without really tasting them. Afterward, I feel so ashamed I make myself vomit. It’s not something I plan, but the guilt is unbearable. I don’t know if I’m underweight—I haven’t had a proper check-up. The scale fluctuates, but I tell myself I’m just being careful. I just want control. But some days, I don’t recognize myself in the mirror.
D021-D022_h001.options:
A. Bulimia Nervosa
    B. Anorexia Nervosa
    C. Adjustment Disorder
    D. Binge-Eating Disorder
D021-D022_h001.answer: B & A. Anorexia Nervosa & Bulimia Nervosa

D021-D022_h002.question:
I’ve been keeping an eye on my weight for a while now—probably the last six months or so. I don’t know, maybe longer. I’ve always been lean from the job, climbing in and out of the crane, working long shifts, but lately… I’ve been more aware of every pound. I step on the scale every morning, even before I shower. If it goes up even a little, it sticks with me all day—makes me jittery, unfocused. So I just… stop eating. Breakfast? Skipped. Lunch? Not hungry. Sometimes dinner too.  

I do eat big meals sometimes—really big—where I feel like I can’t stop, especially late at night when I’m alone. Afterward, I feel so guilty, so full, like I messed up everything. I’ve made myself throw up a few times, not often, but enough to know it’s wrong. I haven’t told my wife. She’s asked why I’m so quiet, why I’m always changing clothes, checking mirrors.  

I’m not sure how much I weigh exactly—under my old weight, I think. But I wouldn’t say I’m dangerously low. I feel okay, mostly. Just… never quite in control.
D021-D022_h002.options:
A. Bulimia Nervosa
    B. Anorexia Nervosa
    C. Adjustment Disorder
    D. Binge-Eating Disorder
D021-D022_h002.answer: B & A. Anorexia Nervosa & Bulimia Nervosa

D021-D022_h003.question:
I’ve always been careful about what I eat—being a nurse, you pay attention to health. But lately, it’s become… more. I can’t bring myself to eat bread, pasta, anything with carbs, really. Fats scare me too—just looking at butter makes me anxious. It’s not about taste; it’s the thought of it turning into weight, immediately. I don’t know why, but I feel like one bite will balloon me up.

I’ve been losing weight, yes—my rings are loose, and my clothes hang off me—but I’m not sure exactly how much. I avoid stepping on the scale at home, and at work, I never use the clinic’s. I tell myself I’m staying healthy, not restricting, but… I do skip meals. Sometimes I’ll eat nothing all day, then, in the evening, I lose control. I might eat half a loaf of bread, cheese, sweets—fast, like I can’t stop. Afterward, I feel so panicked, so disgusted, I make myself throw up.

It’s been going on for months. I’m ashamed, but I can’t seem to break the cycle. I function at work, but I’m tired. Not sure how much longer I can keep this quiet.
D021-D022_h003.options:
A. Bulimia Nervosa
    B. Anorexia Nervosa
    C. Adjustment Disorder
    D. Binge-Eating Disorder
D021-D022_h003.answer: B & A. Anorexia Nervosa & Bulimia Nervosa

D021-D022_h004.question:
I’ve been really struggling lately—probably the last four or five months. I’m constantly aware of what I’m eating, and honestly, I end up skipping meals without even thinking about it. Breakfast is usually too early, lunch gets lost in meetings, and sometimes dinner feels... unnecessary. I’ve always liked feeling lean, but now I just can’t settle unless I’m lighter. The thought of gaining even a couple pounds makes my chest tighten. I weigh myself daily, and if the number goes up, I restrict even more the next day.

There are times—maybe once a week—where I lose control. I’ll eat a lot in a short time, way more than I want to, and afterward, I feel panicked. I’ve made myself throw up a few times, not regularly, but enough that I know how easy it is to do. It’s not something I’m proud of, but it feels like the only way to “fix” it. My wife’s noticed I disappear after meals, and she’s worried, but I tell her I’m fine. I don’t know if I’m underweight—I haven’t had it officially checked—but I feel like I’m still too heavy. I just can’t seem to stop this cycle, but I also can’t let go of needing to stay tight, controlled.
D021-D022_h004.options:
A. Bulimia Nervosa
    B. Anorexia Nervosa
    C. Adjustment Disorder
    D. Binge-Eating Disorder
D021-D022_h004.answer: B & A. Anorexia Nervosa & Bulimia Nervosa

D021-D022_h005.question: I’ve always been careful about what I eat, but lately it’s been harder to manage. I don’t eat much during the day—maybe a few bites at dinner, if that. High-calorie stuff, like pasta or anything with oil, scares me. I feel like just one bite will sit on me, show on my body right away. I record voiceovers from home, so I can schedule around my energy, but some days I’m so drained, my voice sounds weak, and clients notice. I’ve lost a little weight and honestly, I think I need to lose a bit more to feel in control. That said, sometimes I’ll eat a whole meal—more than I plan—especially late at night, and after, I just… get rid of it. Not all the time, but enough that I feel stuck. I don’t know if I’m eating *too little* or *too erratically*. I can’t tell if I’m underweight—my clothes fit loosely, but I don’t track numbers. It’s just that nothing ever feels like enough, and then right after, it feels like too much.
D021-D022_h005.options:
A. Bulimia Nervosa
    B. Anorexia Nervosa
    C. Adjustment Disorder
    D. Binge-Eating Disorder
D021-D022_h005.answer: B & A. Anorexia Nervosa & Bulimia Nervosa

D021-D022_h006.question:
I’ve been on the road a lot—driving trucks for the past twenty years, alone most days. Honestly, I never paid much attention to eating. I just… don’t feel like I need much. I grab a coffee in the morning, maybe a protein bar if I’m hungry, but meals? They feel unnecessary. I’ve lost weight over the past several months—friends have noticed, even my ex-wife called me out on it. But I feel fine. A little lightheaded sometimes, especially after climbing down from the cab, and my hair’s been thinning. I just chalk it up to stress or aging.

There are times, though—long stretches on the highway late at night—when I’ll pull over and eat. A lot. Fast food, sweets, whole bags of chips. More than I should. And afterward… I feel so guilty, so out of control, that I make myself throw it up. I know it’s not great, but it’s the only way I feel like I can reset. I don’t do it every time, but often enough. I don’t know if it’s a problem, really. I’m just trying to manage. The scale keeps going down, but I don’t see the harm. I’ve always worked better lean.
D021-D022_h006.options:
A. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    B. Schizophrenia
    C. Anorexia Nervosa
    D. Bulimia Nervosa
D021-D022_h006.answer: C & D. Anorexia Nervosa & Bulimia Nervosa

D021-D022_h007.question:
I’ve always prided myself on discipline—running a small company, supporting my family, staying sharp. Lately, though, that control feels like it’s slipping, even though I’m doing everything “right.” I track every calorie; I allow myself very little, maybe 800–900 a day, mostly protein and greens. I’ve lost weight over the past few months—my wife keeps mentioning how I look thin, clothes hanging off me—but I don’t feel unwell. In fact, I feel more in control than ever.

The thing is, sometimes—maybe twice a week?—I’ll find myself eating a lot at once. Ice cream, bread, things I normally avoid. Afterward, I feel overwhelmed, so I make myself vomit. It’s not something I enjoy or plan, but it helps ease the panic. I know my wife’s worried, and my doctor raised an eyebrow at my labs, but I’m functioning. Business is steady, I’m not tired all the time, and I don’t see the harm in wanting to stay disciplined. I just want to feel like myself again—focused, in charge.
D021-D022_h007.options:
A. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    B. Schizophrenia
    C. Anorexia Nervosa
    D. Bulimia Nervosa
D021-D022_h007.answer: C & D. Anorexia Nervosa & Bulimia Nervosa

D021-D022_h008.question:
I’ve been really focused on my weight lately—I mean, I’ve always stayed pretty lean, but over the past few months, I’ve started being more strict with myself. I’ll skip meals sometimes, especially breakfast or lunch, just because I don’t feel like I “earned” them, you know? Like, if I haven’t been active enough during the day, I tell myself I shouldn’t eat. I’m also trying to lose a little more weight, even though people say I’m already thin. My coworkers at the studio have noticed I never eat with them anymore.  

There are days when I’m working late, tracking audio for bands, and I get really dizzy—like, light-headed during sessions. I’ve lost some hair, too. But I just chalk it up to stress or lack of sleep. It doesn’t feel serious.  

And yeah… I do have moments where I eat a lot at once—like a whole pizza or a bunch of snacks, especially after a long shift—then later, I feel so guilty I’ll make myself vomit. It’s not every time, but it happens. I don’t know if it’s a pattern or just me coping. Honestly, I can’t tell if I’m doing too much or not enough. The scale moves, but I don’t know where it “should” be.
D021-D022_h008.options:
A. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    B. Schizophrenia
    C. Anorexia Nervosa
    D. Bulimia Nervosa
D021-D022_h008.answer: C & D. Anorexia Nervosa & Bulimia Nervosa

D021-D022_h009.question:
I’ve just been trying to eat the way that feels right for me. My doctor keeps saying I need to gain a little, but I’m fine as I am—always have been. I don’t see the point in adding on weight when I feel better keeping it down. I stay away from bread and sweets mostly; they just sit heavy, you know? Light meals feel cleaner.  

They keep bringing up meals in the dining room, and sometimes I’ll take a tray but only eat what I want. Now and then, if it all feels like too much, I might eat a bit more—more than I usually do—and afterward, well, I just feel so full, so sick to my stomach, that I make myself vomit. It’s not every day, just when things feel out of control.  

My daughter comes by and says I’m fading, but I tell her she’s dramatic. I’m 82—of course I’m smaller now. That’s life. The nurses hover, whispering about intake and calories, but I don’t need force-fed. I’m in a home now, but I remember my routines, my dignity. I just want to manage my own body in peace.
D021-D022_h009.options:
A. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    B. Schizophrenia
    C. Anorexia Nervosa
    D. Bulimia Nervosa
D021-D022_h009.answer: C & D. Anorexia Nervosa & Bulimia Nervosa

D021-D022_h010.question:
I’ve been feeling off for a few months now—maybe six? I can’t say exactly. As an elevator tech, I’m on my feet all day, crawling through shafts, lifting tools. It’s demanding, but I’ve always kept up with it. Lately, though, I’ve been skipping meals just to get through the job. Breakfast? I’m never hungry. Lunch gets left in the truck. Sometimes dinner too. It’s not that I’m dieting or anything—I just don’t feel like eating, and honestly, I feel better when I don’t.

I’ve lost a bit of weight, yeah—my clothes are looser—but I’m not underweight or anything extreme. My buddies at work tease me, but I feel fine. Well, mostly. I get dizzy climbing the service ladders sometimes, and my hair’s been thinning. I found a few strands in my helmet last week. Kind of weird, but I figure it’s stress.

There’ve been times—on weekends, when I’m alone—where I eat a huge amount, like a whole pizza, a family pack of chips, anything fast. And after, I feel so guilty I make myself throw up. It’s not regular, just sometimes. I don’t know if it’s a problem. I just want to feel in control.
D021-D022_h010.options:
A. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    B. Schizophrenia
    C. Anorexia Nervosa
    D. Bulimia Nervosa
D021-D022_h010.answer: C & D. Anorexia Nervosa & Bulimia Nervosa

D021-D022_h011.question:
I’ve always been someone who values control—probably because my job at the hospital runs on precision. Lately, though, it feels like the only thing I can really control is what I eat. I track every calorie, and honestly, most days I stay under 800. It’s hard, especially when meetings run late and the cafeteria smells like pizza, but I tell myself it’s discipline.  

I know I’m not heavy—I wear smalls now, and people have even said I look tired—but in the mirror, my stomach looks bloated, like I’ve gained instead of lost. That’s what keeps me pushing to lose more. I’ve started doing laps after dinner, and sometimes, if I feel like I ate too much—even a normal portion—I’ll make myself throw up. It’s not every day, and it doesn’t happen with massive amounts, but… it helps me reset.  

I don’t know if this is an eating disorder. I’m not *that* thin, but I’m not gaining either. And I’m not binging like I see on TV—just small oversteps, followed by overcorrection. I just can’t seem to stop.
D021-D022_h011.options:
A. Generalized Anxiety Disorder
    B. Bulimia Nervosa
    C. Delusional Disorder
    D. Anorexia Nervosa
D021-D022_h011.answer: D & B. Anorexia Nervosa & Bulimia Nervosa

D021-D022_h012.question:
I’ve always prided myself on running a tight ship—my little bakery has been my life since my husband passed. Lately, though, I just don’t have the same energy. I still get up early to knead dough and open on time, but I find myself skipping meals. I don’t feel hungry like I used to. I’ve cut back—maybe just tea and a slice of dry toast in the morning, a small salad later if I remember. I tell myself I don’t need much; less food means less weight to carry around, and honestly, keeping my waistline down makes me feel… in control. Like I’ve still got some discipline left.

I step on the scale every day, and when the number goes down, I feel like I’ve done something right—like I’m still capable, still strong. But some evenings, after closing, I’ll come home and suddenly eat half a pie or a whole batch of cookies—mindlessly, almost like I'm not there. Then I feel so guilty, so disgusted, I make myself… get rid of it. I don’t do it every time, but often enough. I don’t know if I’m underweight—never been to the doctor about it. The apron hides a lot. I just know I can’t stop this cycle, and I don’t know why.
D021-D022_h012.options:
A. Generalized Anxiety Disorder
    B. Bulimia Nervosa
    C. Delusional Disorder
    D. Anorexia Nervosa
D021-D022_h012.answer: D & B. Anorexia Nervosa & Bulimia Nervosa

D021-D022_h013.question:
I’ve been really stressed lately, especially about how I look. I know I’ve lost some weight over the past few months—just kind of happened because I’ve been trying to eat “cleaner.” I cut out carbs completely and I don’t eat anything with fat, like dairy or oils. I tell myself it’s for health, but honestly, I just feel better when I restrict. When I look in the mirror, my stomach looks huge, even though my husband says I’m fine. I don’t feel fine.  

Sometimes I’ll have a moment where I lose control—I’ll eat a lot at once, like a whole box of cookies or a huge plate of pasta, things I normally wouldn’t touch. Afterward, I feel so guilty, so I make myself throw up. It’s not something I do every time, but often enough that I know it’s not right. I don’t know if I’m bingeing because I’m too strict, or if the purging is making me want to restrict more.  

I’m still within a normal weight range, I think—I haven’t stepped on a scale in a while—but clothes are getting looser. I can’t tell if I’m actually overweight or just seeing it wrong. It’s affecting my focus at work; typing numbers all day used to be easy, but now I’m distracted, counting calories in my head instead.
D021-D022_h013.options:
A. Generalized Anxiety Disorder
    B. Bulimia Nervosa
    C. Delusional Disorder
    D. Anorexia Nervosa
D021-D022_h013.answer: D & B. Anorexia Nervosa & Bulimia Nervosa

D021-D022_h014.question:
I’ve been struggling lately, honestly. I watch what I eat pretty closely because of my job—I’m a gym instructor, so people look up to me to stay in shape. But lately, it feels like no matter how much I work out or how strict I am, I still see myself as... off. When I look in the mirror, my stomach looks huge, even though my coworkers tell me I’m lean. I only eat tiny amounts during the day—sometimes just a few bites at meals—because I get so anxious about gaining weight.  

But then, some nights, I lose control. I’ll end up eating a lot—way more than I should—in secret, like a whole pizza or bags of snacks. Afterward, I feel so guilty that I make myself throw up or do extra cardio to “fix” it. It’s not every day, but it’s been happening regularly for a few months now.  

I’ve lost some weight, but I’m not sure exactly how much. I avoid stepping on the scale. I just know my clothes are looser, and I’m not sure if that’s good or bad anymore. I keep thinking I need to get tighter, more defined, but I’m exhausted all the time.
D021-D022_h014.options:
A. Generalized Anxiety Disorder
    B. Bulimia Nervosa
    C. Delusional Disorder
    D. Anorexia Nervosa
D021-D022_h014.answer: D & B. Anorexia Nervosa & Bulimia Nervosa

D021-D022_h015.question:
I’ve been really stressed lately—school’s demanding, and we’re constantly around food, but I’m not like the other students. I can’t help but feel like I’m losing control, so I’ve started cutting out certain things—no carbs, no fats, nothing that might “slow me down” or make me feel heavy. I tell myself it’s about being disciplined, not about looks, but… sometimes when I look in the mirror, my reflection doesn’t match how I feel. My stomach looks huge, even though people say I’ve lost weight.

I’ve been losing a little here and there—maybe a pound a week? I don’t track it exactly. I just know my pants are looser, and I feel stronger when I resist. But then, some nights, I’ll find myself eating a whole loaf of bread or finishing a batch of pastry dough—stuff I’d normally never touch. Afterward, I feel so guilty, like I ruined everything. I make myself throw up sometimes, just to fix it. It’s not every day. It’s not like I’m doing it all the time. But it happens enough that I’m scared it’s becoming a pattern. I don’t know if I’m just being careful or if I’m actually slipping.
D021-D022_h015.options:
A. Generalized Anxiety Disorder
    B. Bulimia Nervosa
    C. Delusional Disorder
    D. Anorexia Nervosa
D021-D022_h015.answer: D & B. Anorexia Nervosa & Bulimia Nervosa

D021-D022_h016.question:
I’ve always been particular about food, but it’s gotten harder to manage lately. I skip meals sometimes—especially breakfast, since I’m rushing to get to school on time, and honestly, it just feels easier not to eat. Lunch depends; if the cafeteria feels overwhelming, I’ll just grab a black coffee and call it enough. I keep thinking that if I eat anything with real calories—like pizza or pasta—it’ll go straight to my waistline, even if I’ve barely eaten all day. So I avoid those things, mostly stick to salads or plain chicken.  

Over the past few months, I’ve lost a bit of weight, not on purpose exactly, but I haven’t stopped it either. My jeans fit looser, and people have noticed, but I don’t feel underweight—just careful. There are times, though, usually late at night after grading papers, when I get this urge, this kind of numb hunger that turns into eating whatever’s in the kitchen—snacks, bread, sweets. And afterward… I feel so guilty. Sometimes I make myself throw up, or I’ll over-exercise the next morning. It’s not every day, but often enough that I know it’s a problem. I just don’t know if it’s *that* kind of problem.
D021-D022_h016.options:
A. Bipolar II Disorder
    B. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    C. Anorexia Nervosa
    D. Bulimia Nervosa
D021-D022_h016.answer: C & D. Anorexia Nervosa & Bulimia Nervosa

D021-D022_h017.question:
I’ve always been careful about what I eat, but over the past few months, I’ve had to get stricter—there’s so much pressure at work to look put together, especially when I’m on the floor managing staff and dealing with customers. I run a department in a busy store, so I’m on my feet all day, and I just can’t let myself… slump. I keep my meals small—usually under 800 calories, sometimes less if I’ve had a heavy lunch event or a fitting. I track everything. 

The truth is, I get really anxious when I think about gaining weight. Even a pound shows to me, and I start feeling out of control. But some nights, I’ll eat a large amount all at once—boxes of crackers, candy, whatever’s around—then I’ll make myself vomit afterward. I don’t do it every time, but often enough that I notice. I wouldn’t say I’m underweight, but I’m not where I used to be. My clothes fit looser, and people have asked if I’m okay. I just tell them I’ve been busy. The cycle feels hard to stop, like I’m fighting with myself all the time.
D021-D022_h017.options:
A. Bipolar II Disorder
    B. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    C. Anorexia Nervosa
    D. Bulimia Nervosa
D021-D022_h017.answer: C & D. Anorexia Nervosa & Bulimia Nervosa

D021-D022_h018.question:
I’ve always been particular about my eating, but lately it’s gotten to the point where I’m counting every calorie like it’s part of the auction—each one up for bid. I run a fast-paced auction house, and with all the public speaking, I don’t want to feel sluggish or bloated, so I’ve stuck to plain salads, broth, black coffee—nothing over 800 calories a day, maybe. High-calorie foods scare me, honestly. Even a piece of bread feels like it’ll sit on my hips instantly.  

I’ve lost some weight over the past few months—I’m not heavy, that’s for sure—but my wife keeps saying I look too thin, and she’s been pushing me to eat. I can’t bring myself to gain it back, though. Something about it feels dangerous.  

And… there are times—maybe once a week when I’m stressed before a big sale—where I’ll eat a lot in one sitting, fast, like I’m out of control. Pastries, snacks, whatever’s nearby. Then I feel so guilty, so panicked, that I make myself sick afterward. I know it’s not right, but it’s the only way I feel like I can reset. It’s not every day, but often enough that I’m starting to wonder if I’ve lost control.
D021-D022_h018.options:
A. Bipolar II Disorder
    B. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    C. Anorexia Nervosa
    D. Bulimia Nervosa
D021-D022_h018.answer: C & D. Anorexia Nervosa & Bulimia Nervosa

D021-D022_h019.question:
I’ve been a forest ranger for over forty years, and out in the woods, you learn to get by with what you’ve got. Since my wife passed, eating just hasn’t been much of a priority. Mornings especially—no use fussing over breakfast when you’re on patrol by first light. I’ll skip that meal, and if the day runs long, sometimes lunch gets missed too. Evenings, I might eat a small bowl of soup, but anything heavy sits with me, makes me feel sluggish. 

I used to enjoy food—her cooking, especially—but now, anything with fat or sugar, I get anxious. Like if I eat a cookie, I’ll pack it on instantly. I know that sounds irrational, but I can’t shake the feeling. 

There are times—after I’ve gone too long without eating—I get so hungry I’ll stop at a diner and order too much. Then I feel awful, ashamed. I make myself sick after, not every time, but now and then. It’s not… regular. I don’t count calories or weigh myself daily. I don’t know what my weight’s doing exactly—might’ve thinned out a bit, people say I look “fit,” but I feel mostly fine. Just… out of sorts with food.
D021-D022_h019.options:
A. Bipolar II Disorder
    B. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    C. Anorexia Nervosa
    D. Bulimia Nervosa
D021-D022_h019.answer: C & D. Anorexia Nervosa & Bulimia Nervosa

D021-D022_h020.question:
I’ve always been mindful about eating, but over the past few months, it’s gotten harder to ignore the numbers—on the scale, on the food labels, in my head. I skip breakfast most days; sometimes lunch too, especially if I know I’ll be at a home visit where food’s around. I work with families, you know? I can’t be seen picking at a sandwich while a kid is finally eating something hot. But honestly, the thought of eating something like pasta or dessert—anything with real calories—makes me anxious. I get this tight feeling, like if I eat it, the weight will just… stick right away.

There have been times—more than I’d like to admit—where I eat something and then feel so out of control that I make myself throw up. It’s not regular, not planned, but it happens when I feel “full” in a way that scares me. I don’t know how much weight I’ve lost exactly—my husband noticed my rings were loose, and my clothes hang differently. But I haven’t been to the doctor recently, so I can’t say where I stand. I just know I can’t seem to stop this cycle.
D021-D022_h020.options:
A. Bipolar II Disorder
    B. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    C. Anorexia Nervosa
    D. Bulimia Nervosa
D021-D022_h020.answer: C & D. Anorexia Nervosa & Bulimia Nervosa

D021-D022_h021.question:
I’ve just turned 44 this year, and between teaching full days and getting my kids off to school, I feel like I’m barely keeping up. I’ve never been someone who eats much in the morning—never felt hungry, really—and lately, lunch tends to get pushed aside with all the grading and meetings. I’ll admit, I’ve been avoiding anything I think is high in calories—like pasta, desserts, or even oils—because I get this immediate anxiety that if I eat them, I’ll gain weight fast. It’s not that I think I’m fat, but I just can’t shake the feeling that losing control with food would be… dangerous.

There are times when I do eat a lot all at once—more than I mean to—usually late at night when no one’s around. Afterward, I feel so guilty I’ll sometimes make myself vomit, though not every time. My wife’s mentioned I look thinner, but I tell her I’m just stressed or busy. Honestly, I don’t see it as a big health issue. I feel fine—just tired sometimes, and maybe a little lightheaded, but nothing I can’t handle.
D021-D022_h021.options:
A. Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
    B. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    C. Bulimia Nervosa
    D. Anorexia Nervosa
D021-D022_h021.answer: D & C. Anorexia Nervosa & Bulimia Nervosa

D021-D022_h022.question:
I’ve always been careful about my eating, but over the past few months, I’ve had to get stricter—more disciplined. As a dermatologist, I see patients worried about their skin, their appearance, and I feel like I should set an example. So, I track everything I eat, and most days I keep it under 800 calories. I exercise after work, even when I’m tired. 

The truth is, the idea of gaining weight terrifies me. Not like a normal worry—this feels deeper. Even when someone compliments me on how I look, all I can think about is the fat I *must* be hiding. I’ll stand in front of the mirror and pinch my waist, convinced I’m larger than I appear. My husband says I’m too thin, that I look tired, but I don’t see it. I feel fine—just focused.

Lately, though… there have been these moments. Late at night, I’ll eat a lot—way too much—cereal, bread, sweets. And afterward, I panic. I make myself vomit, just to reset. It’s not something I do every day, but often enough that I notice it. I don’t know if it’s a problem, really. I manage my practice, my marriage, my life. It just feels like… part of staying in control.
D021-D022_h022.options:
A. Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
    B. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    C. Bulimia Nervosa
    D. Anorexia Nervosa
D021-D022_h022.answer: D & C. Anorexia Nervosa & Bulimia Nervosa

D021-D022_h023.question:
I’ve always been careful about what I eat, but lately, it’s been harder to manage. As someone who’s supposed to lead teams and stay sharp, I noticed that if I skip breakfast and lunch, I actually feel more focused—less sluggish. I don’t do it every day, but most days, yeah, I just… don’t eat. When I do eat, I get really anxious about anything with fat or sugar—like, if I have a sandwich with mayo or a piece of cake, I convince myself I’ll gain weight overnight. It feels irrational, I know, but the worry’s always there.

There are times, though—usually late at night—when I lose control. I’ll eat a lot of food, fast, like an entire pizza or a bunch of snacks, and then feel terrified afterward. I’ve made myself throw up a few times, not regularly, but enough that I know how easy it is to fall into that cycle. I don’t think I’m underweight, at least no one’s said that, but I don’t track my weight either. Honestly, I don’t think it’s that serious. I can stop any time. I just want to feel in control.
D021-D022_h023.options:
A. Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
    B. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    C. Bulimia Nervosa
    D. Anorexia Nervosa
D021-D022_h023.answer: D & C. Anorexia Nervosa & Bulimia Nervosa

D021-D022_h024.question:
I’ve always been someone who stuck to a routine, even with food—especially now. At work, I’m on my feet for twelve-hour shifts, patrolling the warehouse, so I used to eat enough to keep going. But over the last year or so, I started cutting back… not on purpose, exactly. I just got it in my head that carbs would slow me down, make me gain weight. So I stopped eating bread, potatoes, rice—anything that felt heavy. My wife worries, says I look thin, but I feel fine. Okay, maybe a little dizzy sometimes, especially when I stand up fast, and my skin’s drier than it used to be. I’ve noticed more hair in the shower drain, but I figure that’s just getting older.

I do have these episodes—maybe once or twice a week—where I’ll eat too much, like a whole sandwich, some chips, even ice cream, and afterward… I feel panicked. Like I’ve ruined something. So I make myself throw up. I know it sounds bad, but it’s the only way to reset. I don’t do it every day. I’m not underweight—well, I don’t think so. My uniform still fits the same.
D021-D022_h024.options:
A. Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
    B. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    C. Bulimia Nervosa
    D. Anorexia Nervosa
D021-D022_h024.answer: D & C. Anorexia Nervosa & Bulimia Nervosa

D021-D022_h025.question:
I’ve always been careful about what I eat, but lately it’s gotten harder to manage. I run my own jewelry business from home, and with everything I’ve got on my plate—designs, deadlines, being a single mom sometimes—I don’t have much time or energy to think about meals. I try to keep it under 800 calories a day—just salads, tea, maybe a piece of fruit. Anything more and I start worrying, obsessing really, about putting on weight. I *hate* the idea of getting fat—it scares me more than I can explain.

My daughter says I look too thin, and my doctor brought it up last time, but they don’t get it. I’m not underweight—well, I don’t *think* so—and I exercise just enough to feel in control.  

But sometimes… sometimes I lose that control. Late at night, after a bad day or when a commission falls through, I’ll eat whatever’s in the house—crackers, chocolate, anything. And then I just feel so guilty, so panicked, that I make myself throw up. I know it’s not great, but it’s not like I do it all the time. Not enough to mean something’s really wrong, right?
D021-D022_h025.options:
A. Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
    B. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    C. Bulimia Nervosa
    D. Anorexia Nervosa
D021-D022_h025.answer: D & C. Anorexia Nervosa & Bulimia Nervosa
